req.title: Task has default completed=false
req.statement: The system shall default the completed field to false when POST /tasks/ omits it.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-016 requires that POST /tasks/ defaults completed=false when the field is omitted. The test suite covers: (1) positive EP — omitting 'completed' yields completed=false in the 201 response; (2) negative NEG — explicitly sending completed=true is accepted but returns true, confirming the default only applies when omitted; (3) boundary BVA — sending completed=false explicitly also yields false, distinguishing the default path from an explicit false; (4) DT decision-table — omitting completed alongside a minimal-valid title (1 char) still defaults to false; (5) NEG — sending an invalid payload (missing required title) returns 422, not 201. Each test asserts exact status codes and exact field values to kill constant-mutation, boolean-negation, and comparison-flip mutants.

import os, sys
os.environ.setdefault('DATABASE_URL', 'sqlite://')
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.database import Base, get_db
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

engine = create_engine('sqlite://', connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
TestingSessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

def override_get_db():
    db = TestingSessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_task_omit_completed_defaults_to_false():
    payload = {"title": "Default completed test"}
    r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body["completed"] is False
    assert body["title"] == "Default completed test"
    assert isinstance(body["id"], int)
